FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

An improving Eintracht Frankfurt side travel to Stuttgart this weekend as both sides search for a victory to help their European qualification aspirations in the Bundesliga.

Match News and Current Form

After losing 2-0 to Inter Milan in midweek UEFA Champions League action, Stuttgart will be hoping to bounce back this weekend and extend a three-match unbeaten run in the Bundesliga (W2, D1). The Swabians’ chances of returning to Europe’s top table next term look bleak at this early stage given that they trail the top four by eight points, with defeats in two of their last three home league fixtures (W1) a big reason why that margin is so big. The Swabians have at least kept back-to-back clean sheets in the Bundesliga, and now go in search of a third on the spin in the top-flight for the first time since May 2018. 

Eintracht Frankfurt start the round one place and two points above their hosts, a position they’ve earned by winning three of their last five Bundesliga matches (D1, L1). Quick starters this campaign, the Eagles would be sat in the top two if matches finished at half-time, but an inability to stay the course has seen them drop nine points from winning positions this term. Boss Adi Hütter will also remain concerned about his side’s away form, as Frankfurt have won just two of their last 16 league fixtures on the road (D7, L7), losing two of their last three without scoring. 

Head-to-Head History

Stuttgart are looking to win successive Bundesliga home games against Frankfurt for the first time since February 2010 after a 3-2 victory in last season’s corresponding fixture.

Win Probability
Opta by StatsPerform
Hot Stats and Streaks

Only two of Stuttgart’s last seven Bundesliga games saw both teams score.

Stuttgart have scored first in three of their four home league fixtures this season.

Frankfurt have kept just one clean sheet across their last 24 Bundesliga away matches.

Frankfurt have scored a pre-round league-high six goals on or before the 15th minute this term.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Stuttgart’s Deniz Undav has four goals in five prior H2Hs, all of which came before half-time, with each of his scoring displays therein ending in victory. Frankfurt’s Ritsu Dōan has six goal contributions across nine meetings with Stuttgart, while four of his last six league goals served as match openers.

Stuttgart look to have no fresh injury concerns, while Frankfurt’s Can Uzun could be in contention here after illness.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre. 

Betting Analysis

With both sides quite evenly matched heading into this fixture, the draw market could prove an enticing option. 

Author: Nathan Evans
